summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing throughput and latency vs the incumbent. Redwood demoed recent routing tweaks and quantization tradeoffs, discussed p99 tail spikes under burst and cold-starts, and agreed next steps: run targeted p99 tests, share routing policy and cost model, and ingest representative prompts for final tuning.
topics: Throughput with 2x concurrent streams and batching
Warm vs cold KV cache impact
transcript:
00:00 Marcus Lee: ok folks uh thanks for joining, this is Marcus from Redwood, we have Priya and Daniel here from our side. How's everyone?
00:08 Sophie Tran: good thanks Marcus, i think we have everybody on our side, Rita just hopped on a minute late.
00:15 Evan Moore: morning all, Evan here. Looking forward to seeing the numbers.
00:20 Marcus Lee: great, quick agenda: quick readout of week 4 bench numbers vs your baseline, then routing + quantize notes, then q&a and next steps.
00:35 Priya Kapoor: i'll share screen now, sorry if the auto transcribed name looks weird, let me pull the spreadsheet.
00:44 [screen share start]
00:50 Priya Kapoor: ok first slide, p50/p95/p99 across 256/512 token scenarios. P50 is pretty even, p95 we see a 10-15% delta in favor of Redwood, p99 though, that is the key, we saw spikes up to 420ms compared to the incumbent's 360ms in the 512 token cold start runs.
01:20 Sophie Tran: can you clarify cold start? like new model load or new shard?
01:25 Priya Kapoor: yeah cold meaning KV cache empty plus a fresh worker after autoscale - so initial generation includes extra GC and kernel warmup. Warm runs where KV cache is primed have p99 closer to 320ms.
01:38 Evan Moore: and what was the batch size during those runs?
01:42 Priya Kapoor: batches of 4 for the 2 concurrent streams test; we also ran continuous-batch tests where we allow batching to ramp.
01:50 Marcus Lee: just to note, those cold start p99s are reproducible only under the burst scenario - under reserved slots with pre-warmed workers we keep p99 below incumbent in our config.
02:03 Rita Gomez: (on speaker) our main concern is tail latency during peak 7-9am window, that directly affects SLA to our customers.
02:12 Marcus Lee: absolutely, and that's why we proposed the reserved burst mix last week.
02:17 Priya Kapoor: next slide shows throughput: with our deduped KV cache and continuous batching we sustain 550 reqs/sec for short form prompts (avg 128 tokens) vs incumbent at 420 reqs/sec on same GPU type. For 512 tokens throughput drops to ~120 rps with Redwood vs 95 rps incumbent.
02:45 Sophie Tran: those numbers look promising, what's the token/unit cost delta?
02:50 Marcus Lee: rough numbers on the sheet: unit token cost is about 22% lower on our hosted config assuming steady state reserved capacity; with burst pricing it's closer to 12%. We'll send a more detailed cost projection.
03:05 Evan Moore: is that with quantization applied?
03:08 Priya Kapoor: yes, we tested both fp16 and 4-bit quant profiles. 4-bit gives ~18% cost reduction and increased throughput but p99 can shift by ~30-50ms depending on prompt length. For some of your sensitive pathways we recommend mixed approach: fp16 for high-SLA routes, 4-bit for lower-SLA batched jobs.
03:28 Sophie Tran: got it. What about model fidelity regressions we should expect when switching to 4-bit? Any evals?
03:34 Marcus Lee: we ran a small eval on your supplied prompt set; delta in rouge/accuracy was tiny for completion style tasks but more audible for multi-step reasoning prompts. We'll include the eval artifacts.
03:45 Evan Moore: did you test with KV prefix caching disabled? our current infra doesn't maintain long term KV across instances easily.
03:52 Priya Kapoor: yes we did a run with no KV cache and saw a throughput drop ~38% and p99 increased ~120ms across the board. That's in the cold-run numbers.
04:05 Rita Gomez: are you seeing any retries or non-deterministic errors during stress?
04:10 Priya Kapoor: a few transient 503s during our extreme burst tests when the autoscaler thresholds were hit very quickly, but we have fallback routing to a smaller-capacity model and that eliminates errors at the application level.
04:21 Marcus Lee: for production-facing path we recommend a canary and fallback to a lower-cost model rather than returning error; that's in the playbook.
04:28 Sophie Tran: can you show the breakpoint where you switch routing?
04:32 Priya Kapoor: sure pulled that up, it's the routing policy we pushed last week. Thresholds are p95 > 250ms triggers additional dedicated slot allocation, p99 > 400ms triggers immediate fallback to small variant and a telemetry alert to your ops.
04:48 Evan Moore: is that configurable via API? we need to integrate with our SRE tooling.
04:53 Marcus Lee: yes it's exposed in the control plane API, we'll send the JSON policy.
05:00 Sophie Tran: let's talk about the incumbent comparison - which instance types were you comparing on?
05:06 Priya Kapoor: we matched hardware to the extent possible: A100 equivalent; same tokenization and batching heuristics. The incumbent numbers were provided by AetherBridge's benchmark sheet and re-run by us for parity. There may be slight differences due to kernel versions.
05:24 Evan Moore: there were a few places where the incumbent had better p99 on 512 tokens; any idea why?
05:29 Priya Kapoor: likely due to their model sharding and fewer context switches in their runtime - they use a dedicated microshard model. Our runtime's continuous batching can introduce additional scheduling jitter at extreme tail - we're tuning the kernel dispatch and hope to shave that down.
05:46 Marcus Lee: Priya and our infra team identified a micro-optimization in kernel launch that should reduce p99 by ~30-40ms in these cases; Priya will run it on Wednesday in the lab.
05:55 Sophie Tran: ok that would be great.
06:00 [15:30 marker redacted — meeting progressed with detailed bench walkthroughs, references to shared sheet and logs]
06:10 Priya Kapoor: jumping ahead, we ran a 2-hour soak test with mixed prompt distribution 60/40 short/long; sustained throughput remained within 5% of peak for the first 90 minutes then we saw a small degradation tied to memory leak in our early runtime build; that patch is in QA and we expect it out in staging tomorrow.
06:34 Evan Moore: that leak is the main risk for long running jobs - good to know it's being patched.
06:40 Marcus Lee: we'll update the incident note in the bench spreadsheet.
06:44 Rita Gomez: SSO and audit logs question — for private deployment we need audit logs retained 2 years.
06:51 Daniel Ortiz: yes our private deployment supports customizable retention, and we integrate with your KMS for key rotation. We'll attach the SOC2/ISO summary and audit log config doc.
07:02 Sophie Tran: perfect. Also can we get a sample of the p99 raw traces?
07:06 Priya Kapoor: yes i'll upload the raw traces and timeline, note that some IDs are redacted.
07:11 Evan Moore: for the head-to-head, can you run one more config: reserved capacity + pre-warmed KV + fp16 quant, and send p50/p95/p99 and distribution histograms?
07:20 Priya Kapoor: yes that is doable, will run today and share by Friday morning.
07:24 Marcus Lee: timing wise, if those numbers look good and p99 aligns or beats incumbent in pre-warm config then we can sign off on a 3-month pilot on Dedicated capacity.
07:34 Rita Gomez: what's your estimate of cost delta for dedicated? we have to present this to finance.
07:39 Marcus Lee: ballpark: dedicated reserved slots with our recommended autoscale policy is about 15-18% cheaper per unit vs incumbent's reserved offer at your current utilization. We'll produce an itemized projection in the pricing sheet.
07:51 Sophie Tran: ok, regarding compliance we also asked about data residency for EU traffic. Any blockers?
07:57 Daniel Ortiz: we have EU region private deploy options and can pin traffic regionally; we'll include the deployment topology options in the doc pack.
08:06 Evan Moore: one operational ask: can you expose per-route token breakdowns so we can map cost to features?
08:12 Marcus Lee: yep that's available in Redwood Console, token-level breakdowns per route and per model, we'll enable a view for your team.
08:18 Sophie Tran: perfect. quick question — when you did the 4-bit runs did you also compare hallucination rate on our synthesis tasks?
08:25 Priya Kapoor: yes we flagged a slight uptick in hallucinations on long multi-step; recommend fp16 on any route that requires high fidelity, and 4-bit on bulk lower-risk transformations.
08:36 Sophie Tran: understood.
08:38 Marcus Lee: ok we're nearing the end, want to recap next steps. Priya will run p99 pre-warmed reserved runs and post raw logs; Marcus will send updated routing JSON and cost sheet; Evan will upload the real prompt bundles; Sophie will schedule finance review for next Tuesday.
08:55 Sophie Tran: yes, i'll send calendar invite for finance review.
09:00 Marcus Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the shared folder and Slack channel.
09:05 [screen share end]
09:10 Marcus Lee: meeting adjourned.
notes: Shared artifacts: bench spreadsheet (link in chat), routing policy JSON (to be posted), SOC2 summary and audit-log config doc
